content.text:
I refactored the crate in eight commits, and the tests pass after each one. `cargo clippy --all-targets` is clean at the default lint level. I did not change any test, and behavior is unchanged.

| Commit | What changed | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `f0c6928` | Numeric limits moved into a new `limits` module. | Ranges like `0..=43_200` were repeated as literals in several places. |
| `a15060b` | The command name is parsed into a `Command` enum when the request is parsed. | Dispatch matched on string literals and had a catch-all error arm. Unknown names still give `InvalidRequest`. |
| `7ab8b3b` | `MessageId` and `ReceiptHandle` are now their own types in a new `ids` module. | They were bare `u64`s, and the `m-`/`r-` text form and handle parsing were loose functions. |
| `e13b682` | Group id and sequence number are now one `FifoPlace` value on `Message`. | They were two `Option`s that are only ever set together, in a FIFO queue. |
| `ee02fe1` | `SendMessage` is split, with a `SendTarget` enum for standard versus FIFO sends. `push_fifo` returns the sequence number directly. | The old function was long and passed the FIFO ids around as a tuple `Option`. |
| `c290cc2` | The `ContentBasedDeduplication` check is one function shared by create and set. | The same rule was written out in both commands. |
| `8aa9536` | New `required_string` and `required_integer` getters replace `expect("required")`. | The call `params.require(...)` still runs first, because the spec reports missing parameters before wrong types. No handler can panic on missing input now. |
| `81c64ff` | Removed a `usize` cast and an unused closure. `ChangeMessageVisibility` now uses an `expect` that names the invariant. | It no longer silently skips a message that must exist. |

The last commit mixes three small tidy-ups instead of one kind of change, and the message says so.

Two things I left alone on purpose:
- **Queue names:** I did not wrap them in a newtype, because it would touch nearly every signature for little gain.
- **`clippy::pedantic`:** I did not chase its remaining warnings. Most are style preferences, like passing `&u64` or adding `#[must_use]`.
